subject: Proposal: 18/30-month hybrid term with staged uplift and rollback clause
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Proposal: 18/30-month hybrid term with staged uplift and rollback clause

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation I put together an alternative term structure that we think balances AcmeHealth's budgeting horizon and the need for predictable capacity as you bring more feature teams onto the platform. High level:

- Hybrid tenor: 18-month base commitment + optional 12-month extension (customer elects at month 12) to convert to a 30-month total term.
- Staged entitlements: commit expands across three cadence windows (months 1–6 / 7–12 / 13–18) to align with product launches.
- Safety-net rollback: if usage stays below 65% of the committed baseline in months 13–18, a one-time credit (10% of remaining term) can be applied to the following renewal or a partial early-exit without penalty.
- Co-term option: we can align the start date with your current platform contract to simplify procurement and reduce admin overhead.
- Billing: quarterly in arrears, standard payment terms.

I've attached a short proposal and a one-page summary of the rollback mechanics for procurement to review. If this structure looks interesting, I recommend setting a 30-minute call with procurement + engineering to confirm measurement windows and the telemetry signal we'll use for eligibility.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-proposal-hybrid-term-v1.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement review (Lisa/Tom) — confirm auto-renew opt-out language and KMS requirements
2) Legal quick review of rollback clause — Marissa, can you take point?
3) If acceptable, I’ll generate a term sheet and a DocuSign routing order for signature

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,
Priyom

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. High-level Acme feedback: we like the staged uplift concept and an ability to co-term is attractive. A few procurement asks before we take this to legal: 

- Our procurement team generally prefers a 24- or 36-month contractual horizon (for amortization). Is there a way to surface an equivalent 24/36 option with the same staging logic?
- We need an explicit auto-renew opt-out window (we cannot have auto-renew silently extend the term).
- Security: SSO + KMS integration must be in the term sheet; please note our KMS is customer-managed (we will need an appendix).
- Please send an initial estimate of expected quarterly spend for the first 18 months (we need that for capital planning).

Looping in Procurement and Tom who will own the SSO/KMS checklist. If you can send a term-sheet draft and an updated spreadsheet with quarterly cost projections, we can aim to run this through our legal by next Friday.

Thanks,
Lisa
Director of Product Ops, AcmeHealth
